full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
conclusion: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on R^n, and E(t)=∫_{R^n}e(x,t) dx is differentiable with E'(t)=0, where e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². Spatial squares and Laplacian use the Euclidean/Frobenius and componentwise normalizations in the original target; no conclusion is asserted at time zero.

hypotheses.statement: The integers n,m satisfy n≥1 and m≥1, and u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth.
The fixed vector q∈R^m has Euclidean norm |q|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every t>0, |u(x,t)|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every t>0 there exists a real number a with u_tt(x,t)-Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of any choice of a is assumed.
For every pair of real times 0<s<t there is a compact set C⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for all x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

definitions.definition: Xn=ℝ^n with the standard orthonormal coordinates indexed by j=1,…,n, its Euclidean norm and inner product, and its standard topology.

Ym=ℝ^m with its standard Euclidean norm |y|=sqrt(Σ_k y_k²) and real inner product ⟨y,z⟩=Σ_k y_k z_k; k runs from 1 to m. All inner products and vector norms below use the corresponding standard real Euclidean structures.

dx is standard Lebesgue measure on Xn=ℝ^n; ∫_{ℝ^n} f(x) dx denotes its real Lebesgue (Bochner) integral. Integrable means absolute Lebesgue integrability. Totalized integrals used for representation assert no finiteness without a proof.
Ω={(x,t)∈Xn×ℝ : t>0}. Positive-time differentiation means ordinary differentiation in this open domain, with no assertion at t=0.
ũ(x,t)=u(x,t) when t>0 and ũ(x,t)=q when t≤0. This only specifies a total representation of u; no regularity at nonpositive times is asserted.

For real normed spaces A,B, a function f:A→B, a point z∈A and a direction v∈A, write D_v f(z)=Df(z)[v]=fderiv ℝ f z v. Here Df(z) is the continuous linear Fréchet derivative when it exists, and the total fderiv convention gives the zero continuous linear map otherwise. This notation alone asserts no differentiability.

b_std is the standard orthonormal basis; its jth vector, written b_j for j=1,…,n, has jth coordinate 1 and other coordinates 0. Fin n indices 0,…,n−1 are an equivalent relabeling with the same Euclidean structures and volume.

definitions.type: family of constant spatial directions in Xn×ℝ

definitions.definition: On Ω set u_t=D_T ũ, u_tt=D_T(D_T ũ), ∂_{x_j}u=D_{S_j}ũ, ∂_{x_jx_j}u=D_{S_j}(D_{S_j}ũ), and ∂_{x_j}u_t=D_{S_j}(D_T ũ). For any scalar or vector field h on Ω use the same total extension convention (arbitrary off Ω) and write ∂_t h=D_T h and ∂_{x_j}h=D_{S_j}h on Ω. These are derivatives of the original germs wherever differentiable. Δ_xu=Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise, and |D_xu|²=Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|² is the Frobenius square.

binders.type: scalar or vector field on Ω

definitions.definition: For (x,t)∈Ω, e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². The normalization contains no factor 1/2. When a total time function is needed extend e by zero at t≤0.

definitions.type: family of real flux functions on Ω
definitions.definition: flux is the family denoted g_j: for j=1,…,n and (x,t)∈Ω, g_j(x,t)=⟨u_t(x,t),∂_{x_j}u(x,t)⟩. Extend by zero at nonpositive times when total functions are needed.

For t>0, E(t)=∫_{Xn} e(x,t) dx. This definition alone asserts neither integrability nor differentiability. Use the integral of the zero extension of e for a total real-time representation; its restriction is this same energy.

For a scalar or vector function f on a topological space A with a distinguished zero in its codomain, tsupport f is the closure in A of {z : f(z)≠0}. Compact topological support means that this closed set is compact.

binders.type: function on A with zero in its codomain
